title: Naval Topic 4 生词 · 单词卡

cards.ex: Gains are the good things you get, like money, skills or progress. Most of the gains in life means most of the benefits you get. As a verb, gain means to get or increase something.
exs: I've seen big gains since I started working out.
You'll gain more confidence with practice.

src.t: Another one of yours: most of the gains in life come from suffering in the short term so you can get paid in the long term.
src.zh: 你还有一句话：人生中大部分收获，都来自短期的吃苦，这样你才能在长期得到回报。

lg: 一点一点多出来、得到的好东西。

cards.ex: On a daily basis means every day or regularly. Basis here means the way or schedule something happens on. We also say on a weekly or a regular basis.
exs: I talk to clients on a daily basis.
Try to practice on a daily basis, even for five minutes.

src.t: That’s classic. That’s the marshmallow test on a daily basis.
src.zh: 这很经典，就是每天都在做的棉花糖实验。

cards.ex: An addict is someone who can't stop doing something. A suffering addict is someone who starts to need the pain itself, as if pain alone proves you're making progress. Chris says people need to avoid becoming one.
exs: Don't become a suffering addict; rest is part of the plan.
He's a bit of a workout addict.

src.t: But there’s an interesting challenge where I think people need to avoid becoming a suffering addict,
src.ft: But there’s an interesting challenge where I think people need to avoid becoming a suffering addict, sort of using suffering as the proxy for progress as opposed to the outcome of the suffering. Right?
src.zh: 但这里有个有意思的问题，我觉得人们要避免变成一个“吃苦上瘾”的人，就是把吃苦本身当成进步的标志，而不是看吃苦带来的结果。对吧？

lg: 离不开“痛苦”本身，把受苦当成进步的人。

cards.ex: Sort of means kind of or a little. People use it to make a statement softer or less exact. It's extremely common in casual American speech.
exs: I'm sort of hungry, but not really.
It's sort of like a lash lift, but different.

src.t: sort of using suffering as the proxy for progress as opposed to the outcome of the suffering. Right?
src.ft: But there’s an interesting challenge where I think people need to avoid becoming a suffering addict, sort of using suffering as the proxy for progress as opposed to the outcome of the suffering. Right?
src.zh: 但这里有个有意思的问题，我觉得人们要避免变成一个“吃苦上瘾”的人，就是把吃苦本身当成进步的标志，而不是看吃苦带来的结果。对吧？

cards.ex: A proxy is something that stands in for something else. Using suffering as the proxy for progress means treating pain as the sign that you're improving. In business, a proxy can also be a person acting for you.
exs: Hours at work are a bad proxy for how productive you are.
Price isn't always a good proxy for quality.

src.t: sort of using suffering as the proxy for progress as opposed to the outcome of the suffering. Right?
src.ft: But there’s an interesting challenge where I think people need to avoid becoming a suffering addict, sort of using suffering as the proxy for progress as opposed to the outcome of the suffering. Right?
src.zh: 但这里有个有意思的问题，我觉得人们要避免变成一个“吃苦上瘾”的人，就是把吃苦本身当成进步的标志，而不是看吃苦带来的结果。对吧？

lg: 代替真东西站在那里的“替身”。

cards.ex: As opposed to compares two things and says you mean the first, not the second. Here it's pain as a sign of progress, as opposed to the real result. It's a clear way to make a contrast.
exs: I prefer mornings, as opposed to late nights.
Focus on quality, as opposed to quantity.

src.t: sort of using suffering as the proxy for progress as opposed to the outcome of the suffering. Right?
src.ft: But there’s an interesting challenge where I think people need to avoid becoming a suffering addict, sort of using suffering as the proxy for progress as opposed to the outcome of the suffering. Right?
src.zh: 但这里有个有意思的问题，我觉得人们要避免变成一个“吃苦上瘾”的人，就是把吃苦本身当成进步的标志，而不是看吃苦带来的结果。对吧？

lg: 把两样东西放在对立的两边比。

cards.ex: Attached means connected or joined to something. Naval says he had attached his well-being to pain, meaning his happiness was linked to suffering. Attached to can also mean emotionally close.
exs: I'm really attached to my old phone.
Don't attach your self-worth to one client's opinion.

src.t: I have attached well-being and satisfaction to pain, not to what the pain gets me on the other side of it.
src.zh: 我把幸福感和满足感绑在了痛苦上，而不是绑在痛苦最终能带给我的东西上。

lg: 用一根线把两样东西连在一起。

cards.ex: Well-being means being healthy, comfortable and happy, in body and mind. Naval talks about his overall well-being and satisfaction. It's common in health and work talk.
exs: Sleep is so important for your well-being.
The company cares about employee well-being.

src.t: I have attached well-being and satisfaction to pain, not to what the pain gets me on the other side of it.
src.zh: 我把幸福感和满足感绑在了痛苦上，而不是绑在痛苦最终能带给我的东西上。

lg: 身心都舒服、过得好的状态。

cards.ex: Anguish is very strong pain, especially in your mind or heart. Naval says suffering is mostly mental anguish, not physical pain. It's a strong, serious word.
exs: You could see the anguish on his face.
Waiting for the results was pure anguish.

src.t: Suffering is mostly mental anguish and mental pain, and it just means you don’t wanna do the task at hand.
src.zh: 受苦主要是精神上的煎熬和痛苦，说白了就是你不想做眼前这件事。

lg: 心被紧紧揪住的那种痛。

cards.ex: The task at hand is the job you need to do right now. At hand means close or right in front of you. People say focus on the task at hand.
exs: Put your phone away and focus on the task at hand.
Let's get back to the task at hand.

src.t: Suffering is mostly mental anguish and mental pain, and it just means you don’t wanna do the task at hand.
src.zh: 受苦主要是精神上的煎熬和痛苦，说白了就是你不想做眼前这件事。

lg: 现在就摆在你手边、要做的那件事。

cards.ex: Effective means it works well and gets the result you want. Naval asks which is more effective: suffering, or seeing it in a different way. Very common at work and in health.
exs: This cleanser is really effective.
What's the most effective way to learn English?

src.t: and then the question is what’s more effective: to suffer along the way or just to interpret it in a way that it’s not suffering?
src.ft: If you were fine doing the task at hand then you wouldn’t be suffering, and then the question is what’s more effective: to suffer along the way or just to interpret it in a way that it’s not suffering?
src.zh: 如果你乐意做眼前的事，你就不会觉得受苦，那问题就变成了：哪个更有效——一路受着苦，还是换个角度去理解，让它不再是受苦？

lg: 做了一件事以后，真的有结果。

cards.ex: To interpret means to decide what something means, or to explain it in your own way. Interpret it in a way that's not suffering means see the same situation differently. It also means translating speech between languages.
exs: How do you interpret her message?
She interprets for Chinese clients at the clinic.

src.t: and then the question is what’s more effective: to suffer along the way or just to interpret it in a way that it’s not suffering?
src.ft: If you were fine doing the task at hand then you wouldn’t be suffering, and then the question is what’s more effective: to suffer along the way or just to interpret it in a way that it’s not suffering?
src.zh: 如果你乐意做眼前的事，你就不会觉得受苦，那问题就变成了：哪个更有效——一路受着苦，还是换个角度去理解，让它不再是受苦？

lg: 把一件事“翻译”成你自己的理解。

cards.ex: A journey is a long trip, and here it means the whole process of reaching a goal. Successful people say the journey was the fun part, meaning the path, not the finish line. Very common in motivational talk.
exs: Learning English is a journey, not a race.
Enjoy the journey.

src.t: You hear from a lot of successful people, they look back and they say, “Oh the journey was the fun part.”
src.zh: 你会听到很多成功人士回头看时说：“哦，其实过程才是最有趣的部分。”

lg: 从起点走到终点的整个过程。

cards.ex: Entertaining means fun and interesting to watch, do or listen to. Naval says the hard path was actually the entertaining part. We use it for people, shows and stories.
exs: The podcast is really entertaining.
He's an entertaining guy to work with.

src.t: That was actually the entertaining part and I should have enjoyed it more.
src.zh: 那其实才是最好玩的部分，我当时应该更享受它。

cards.ex: A regret is a feeling of being sorry about something you did or didn't do. It's a common regret means many people feel this way. As a verb: I regret not trying.
exs: My only regret is not starting sooner.
You won't regret it.
lg: 回头看时，心里那一声“要是当初……”。
